display_name: K. Seshadri Iyer & Young Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV
one_line: Statesman-dewan and young maharaja of Mysore, pioneers of the Shivanasamudra hydroelectric project powering Kolar Gold Fields and early electrification in Mysore State.

appearance.age_look: Seshadri Iyer appears as a dignified man in his mid‑50s with a slender build, while Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV appears as a composed teenager around 16 with a slightly slighter frame.
appearance.face: Seshadri has an oval face, medium‑brown South Indian complexion, neatly groomed salt‑and‑pepper moustache, sharp nose, thoughtful dark eyes and a calm, focused default expression; Krishnaraja has a softer oval face, slightly lighter brown complexion, clean‑shaven, large earnest eyes and a composed but curious default expression.
appearance.hair: Seshadri’s hair is short, neatly combed back, dark with subtle grey at the temples, mostly concealed beneath a deep‑maroon Mysore-style felt turban with a modest gold edge; Krishnaraja’s hair is black, short and tidily brushed back under a rounded dark‑green silk Mysore turban with a small central gold brooch and a short white plume.
appearance.costume: Seshadri wears a late‑19th‑century Mysore dewan’s outfit: a long knee‑length white cotton angarkha-style coat fastened to the right, over a simple high‑collared off‑white cotton shirt, paired with narrow white churidar trousers and black leather formal shoes; over his shoulders is a plain but elegant dark‑navy wool shawl with a thin gold border, and he wears a practical silver pocket watch chain visible at his waist; Krishnaraja wears a formal royal costume of the same era: a rich dark‑green silk angarkha reaching mid‑calf with subtle woven floral motifs, fastened with small gold buttons, a deep‑red silk sash tied at the waist with its end hanging to his left, off‑white churidar trousers, and pointed brown leather mojari shoes; he has a simple pearl necklace close to the neck, a thin gold bracelet on the right wrist, and a narrow cream shawl with green border draped over his left forearm for ceremony.
appearance.signature: A rolled parchment map of the Shivanasamudra hydroelectric scheme and transmission lines tied with a red ribbon, which Seshadri holds in his left hand while Krishnaraja lightly supports it with his right hand, symbolising their joint role in planning the project.

ref_desc: A dignified mid‑50s Seshadri Iyer with maroon Mysore turban, white angarkha, churidar and navy shawl stands beside teenage Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV in dark‑green silk angarkha, red sash and green turban, both holding a rolled Shivanasamudra project map accented in white, maroon, navy, dark green and gold.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet showing two consistent characters from late‑19th‑century Mysore: first, K. Seshadri Iyer, a dignified man in his mid‑50s with an oval face, medium‑brown complexion, neat salt‑and‑pepper moustache and calm, thoughtful eyes, wearing a deep‑maroon Mysore felt turban with a thin gold edge, a long white cotton angarkha‑style coat over an off‑white high‑collared shirt, narrow white churidar trousers and black leather formal shoes, a simple pocket watch chain at his waist and a dark‑navy wool shawl with a thin gold border over his shoulders; second, young Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, a composed teenager with an oval face, slightly lighter brown complexion and large earnest eyes, black hair brushed back under a rounded dark‑green silk Mysore turban with a small central gold brooch and short white plume, wearing a rich dark‑green silk angarkha with subtle floral motifs and gold buttons, a deep‑red silk sash at the waist with its end hanging to his left, off‑white churidar trousers, pointed brown leather mojari shoes, a simple pearl necklace, a thin gold bracelet on his right wrist and a narrow cream shawl with green border draped over his left forearm; have Seshadri and Krishnaraja standing close together, both modestly and fully clothed, jointly holding a rolled parchment map of the Shivanasamudra hydroelectric project tied with a red ribbon, all rendered with clean shonen‑anime energy but historically grounded costume details and a dominant palette of white, dark green, deep maroon, navy blue and gold.
